trapFamily.trap: vendor shape in the port: the regional blood supplier's order request and receipt (HlOrderRequest with lines of product 'RBC' / abo / rhd 'NEG' / qty, priority 'STAT'; HlOrderReceipt with orderRef and allocations[].qtyAllocated), its allocation status strings ('PART_ALLOCATED', 'BACKORDERED'), its embargo error class (HaemalinkEmbargoError with embargoCode 'REGIONAL_SHORTAGE' / 'TTI_QUARANTINE' and liftsAt) leak into the port and the request service

subGoals.rule: Ports and the application core speak the application's own language: the supplier's request, receipt, field names, product and priority codes, allocation status strings and embargo codes stay in the adapter, and the core states its own outcomes (Cockburn P1: each adapter talks to the application through a port).
The core has no runtime dependency on the vendor SDK: an embargo reaches it as its own error, not as the vendor's error class or its name (Cockburn P1).

precedent: clean-shaped: the existing delivery port (application/needs/Deliveries.ts) is written in the application's own type (DeliveryUpdate with DeliveryState 'being packed' | 'on the way' | 'delivered'), and HaemalinkDeliveries translates from the SDK's consignment(orderRef) record and its stages ('PICKING', 'DISPATCHED', 'DELIVERED', stageAt).

gaming.what: rename: the port declares its own copy of the supplier's order and receipt (SupplyRequest with lines of product / abo / rhd / qty; SupplyReceipt with orderRef and allocations[].qtyAllocated / allocationStatus) under domain-sounding names, the adapter passes the vendor's receipt through, and the service recognises the embargo by the error's name string and reads embargoCode and liftsAt instead of importing the class
